name: Meta
one_liner: Builds Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Threads, Meta AI and Reality Labs; known for fast two-problem LeetCode rounds and, since late 2025, an AI-enabled coding round.

levels.intern: Software Engineer Intern (BS/MS/PhD; also Production Engineer and Network Production Engineer interns). Meta University (the 1st/2nd-year program) closed in 2025.
levels.new_grad: E3 (IC3), posted as 'Software Engineer, University Grad' or similar; Production Engineer new grad is a separate track.
levels.early_career: E3 for 0 to about 2 years; E4 (IC4) typically from about 1 to 2+ years (Levels.fyi E4 data points start at 1 YOE). Some loops evaluate across two levels (E4/E5) based on design and behavioral signal.

process_new_grad.details: About 30 min: background, why Meta, logistics, timeline (Hello Interview E3 guide). Many new grads are contacted after applying with a referral.

CodeSignal, proctored with camera, mic and screen sharing. Two formats reported: (1) since mid-2025, one practical problem in 4 progressive stages in 90 min (e.g. in-memory database, cloud file storage service), unit tests visible, reference docs allowed but no AI or solution searching (Hello Interview; Jun 2025 candidate post on the 'new 4-level' OA); (2) 4 separate LeetCode-style questions (a US E3 new grad offer post, Mar 2025: 1 easy, 2 medium, 1 hard; Hello Interview's alternative format: 4 easy/medium questions in 70 min).

45 min with an engineer in a shared online editor where code is not compiled; typically 2 medium problems, often Meta-tagged LeetCode or close variants; sometimes 1 or 2 short project questions first (Mar 2026 report). Two US E3 offer posts (Jan and Mar 2025) describe going straight from the OA to the 3-round loop with no technical phone screen.

Usually 3 interviews: 2 coding (45 min, about 2 problems each) and 1 behavioral (45 min). Since Oct 2025 one coding round can be the AI-enabled coding round (about 60 min in CoderPad with file explorer, editor and AI chat; multi-file codebase: fix bugs, build a feature, optimize). Hello Interview's AI-enabled post scopes it to E5 to E7 and M2 SWE loops, but its E3 guide says it may replace one of the two E3 coding rounds, and a Bangalore University Grad candidate (Nov 2025) was told the loop was 1 coding + 1 AI-enabled coding + 1 behavioral.

After passing, conversations with potential hiring managers, then offer and negotiation; whole process usually 4 to 12 weeks (Hello Interview E3). Example US E3 (2024 to 2025 cycle): applied with referral Sep 30, 2024, OA Oct 10, all 3 rounds Dec 10, verbal offer Jan 3, 2025, written Jan 13. A Bangalore candidate (Dec 2025) was rejected after the full loop because 'they are out of positions'.

process_intern.details: Meta posts SWE intern roles in the fall; as of Oct 1, 2026 the main Summer 2027 SWE intern requisition had not been posted (Extern; first 2027 req was a Data Engineer intern on Sep 29). Referrals matter; the intern loop is short and standardized (Aced).
CodeSignal, about 70 min, usually 4 questions of increasing difficulty; some candidates also get an optional hour-long scenario-based behavioral survey (Aced intern guide).

Official Meta post (updated Oct 2022): stage one phone screen and stage two interview (video), 'identical expectations', about 5 min intro, 30 to 35 min coding with 'one to two coding questions', then Q&A. 2025 reports: two back-to-back interviews, two Meta-tagged LeetCode problems each (e.g. Kth Missing Positive Number, Interval List Intersections, Custom Sort String, Right Side View). Aced says many recent interns had a single 40-min tech screen after the OA.
Interns are not asked system design. Hiring managers are rarely in the intern loop (Aced). Return offers depend on mentor and manager feedback.

process_experienced_notes: For 1 to 3 years (E4): OA sometimes, phone screen with 2 coding problems, then a full loop; Meta's full loop guide (PDF titled 'SWE _Full Loop_IC4-6') says '4 to 6 of 45 minute interviews' covering coding, design and behavioral. Hello Interview's E4 guide lists 4 onsite rounds: 1 traditional coding, 1 AI-enabled coding (60 min), 1 System Design or Product Architecture, 1 behavioral; 4 to 8 weeks total. A 2026 Bay Area infra loop (5+ YOE candidate) showed 2 design rounds and the recruiter evaluating across E4/E5. A Bangalore 2025 software engineer loop (2.5 YOE candidate, level not stated) added an 'elimination stage': a live DSA interview, a hard 4-question OA, and a Likert-scale behavioral assessment, before a 4-round loop (behavioral, product architecture, AI-enabled coding, pure DSA).
timeline: Typically 4 to 12 weeks from recruiter screen to offer (Hello Interview); E3 example above took about 3.5 months including the holiday period. Phone screen results often within 1 to 6 business days; loop results 1 to 2 weeks. New grad and intern roles post in the fall; Meta University closed (memo Jan 2025). Team matching happens after the loop and can stall when headcount closes, especially in Bangalore.

oa.format: New grad: 90 min, either a single 4-stage progressive practical problem (in-memory DB, file storage service) or 4 independent LeetCode-style questions. Intern: about 70 min, 4 questions of escalating difficulty (Aced). Bangalore E4 2025: hard 4-question OA plus a Likert behavioral assessment.
oa.notes: Correctness per stage matters more than speed; most candidates do not finish all 4 stages (Hello Interview). Reference docs allowed, AI and solution search are not. OA results are weighed with the phone screen.

coding.rounds: New grad: phone screen (sometimes skipped) + 2 coding rounds in the loop, one of which may be AI-enabled. Intern: 1 to 2 coding interviews.
coding.style: LeetCode style, mostly Meta-tagged mediums and their twists (merge two interval lists, left and right side views, calculator with only + and *); about 2 problems per 40 min so speed matters. Meta's full loop guide (IC4 to IC6 version) says 'We do not ask dynamic programming questions'; E3 reports show occasional DP where a recursive solution was accepted.
coding.environment: Shared online editor; 'the interviewer will not compile your code' and Meta's guide tells you to practice 'with just a plain text editor with no compiler, linter, syntax highlighter, autocomplete'. AI-enabled round: CoderPad with a runnable multi-file project and an AI chat (Hello Interview lists GPT-4o mini, GPT-5, Claude Haiku/Sonnet/Opus, Gemini 2.5 Pro and Llama 4 Maverick). Outside the AI round, no outside assistance including AI tools like ChatGPT, and filters (including virtual or blurred backgrounds) must be off (official guide).
coding.graded_on: Four focus areas from Meta's guide: Communication, Problem solving (reasoning, multiple approaches, complexity), Coding (organized, correct structure), Verification (test cases, finding your own bugs). The AI-enabled round is graded on Problem Solving, Code Quality, Verification and Communication (Hello Interview).

system_design: None for E3 new grads and interns. E4 (about 1 to 3 years) adds one design interview: System Design (distributed systems, scale) or Product Architecture (APIs, data models, product features) depending on the role (Meta full loop guide via swe-prep-onsite).

behavioral.framework: Meta values plus five behavioral focus areas: Resolving conflict, Growing continuously, Embracing ambiguity, Driving results, Communicating effectively (Meta full loop guide); STAR recommended
what_they_look_for: Values: Move fast; Build awesome things; Be direct and respect your colleagues; Focus on long-term impact; Live in the future; Meta, Metamates, me
Honest reflection under rapid follow-up questions
How you use AI responsibly to ship faster (2026)
sample_questions: Tell me about the project you are most proud of.
Tell me about a time you disagreed with a design choice. How did it affect the outcome?
Tell me about a time you had limited information and still had to proceed.
What do you feel you lack, and how are you improving it?
Tell me about a conflict with a teammate.
Tell me about a time you had to follow someone else's opinion.
Tell me about a time you used AI to deliver something faster than you otherwise could have.
How do you use AI safely in your day-to-day work?

non_leetcode_formats: AI-enabled coding round (about 60 min): partially built multi-file codebase, often a game or puzzle (candidates and creators describe 'Game of Fifteen' and 'The Puzzle' practice sets); phases are bug fixing, core implementation and optimization; you choose the model; graded on judgment and verification, not prompting. CodeSignal progressive 4-stage OA (build a working system step by step). Product Architecture design round for E4+. Bangalore 2025 Likert-scale behavioral assessment.

reported_questions.title: Convert BST to Sorted Doubly Linked List (in place)
Merge two sorted interval lists (Merge Intervals variation)

Kth Missing Positive Number variant: return the missing number counting from the leftmost element (binary search); asked with the left and right side views variant

reported_questions.role: Software engineer, Bangalore (full loop, pure DSA round; 2.5 YOE)

Making A Large Island
reported_questions.role: Software engineer, Bengaluru phone screen (4+ YOE; asked with Sort Array By Parity)

focus_topics: Arrays and strings with two pointers and hashing
Binary trees: BFS level order, side views, zigzag, diameter, LCA
Stacks and parsing (parentheses, calculators, path simplification)
Graphs and grids: BFS/DFS, islands, shortest exit
Reading and extending an unfamiliar multi-file codebase with an AI assistant
tips: Drill Meta-tagged problems by recent frequency and their known variants; Hello Interview's most common E3 list starts with Basic Calculator II, Valid Word Abbreviation, Valid Palindrome II, Buildings With an Ocean View and Binary Tree Right Side View.
Budget about 15 to 20 minutes per problem: state the approach, get a nod, code, then walk through test cases yourself (no compiler).
Practice coding in a plain text editor with autocomplete off; Meta's guide asks you to practice exactly that.

Prepare for the AI-enabled round: break the task down yourself, give the AI small focused tasks, read and test every chunk, and catch its mistakes; blindly pasting output scores worse than not using AI.
Ask your recruiter which loop format you have (AI-enabled vs two classic coding rounds); Jugal's Jul 2026 post notes recruiters tell candidates in advance.
Prepare 4 to 5 STAR stories mapped to the five focus areas plus one honest story about using AI at work.
For the CodeSignal OA, practice building a small system in stages (key-value store with TTL and versioning) and prioritize passing each stage's tests.
Jugal's Part 1 post (Jul 2025) summarizes Meta prep as graphs and trees, hash tables, two pointers, tries, and production-grade code with edge cases.
compensation_note: Levels.fyi (fetched Oct 4, 2026), US Software Engineer E3: average total comp $181,313 from 42 recent data points; p25 $170,750, median $181,500, p75 $193,400 (page range $152K to $214K+); median base $141,000, median stock $35,000/yr. E4: average $299,140. India IC3 (Bangalore) offers reported Nov 2025 and Jan 2026: base INR 30.87 lakh, 10% bonus, $51K RSUs over 4 years, first-year total about INR 49 to 54 lakh including sign-on and relocation (LeetCode posts).

The AI-enabled round is confirmed by Business Insider (Jul 29, 2025; Meta confirmed) and Wired/404 Media, and Hello Interview dates the rollout to Oct 2025 [VERIFIED secondary].
